fields.description:
## Context / Problem

No workflow step runs `npx playwright install chromium`, so the `browser_runner` fixture
self-skips on "Chromium unavailable" in CI: the browser tier never executes there. A skipped
tier looks exactly like a passing one in the summary, so CI reports green while a whole class
of assertions never ran and nothing tells the reader. Surfaced while implementing bug
`9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091`; pre-existing.

## Decision (recorded by the operator in a comment on this ticket)

**Option (b): the tier is NOT run in CI, and its non-execution becomes explicit and enforced.**
It stays local-only, which is where it was already effectively running. Option (a) —
provisioning Chromium in CI — is rejected on cost (see the operator comment). AC2 of the
original draft, the (a) branch, is dropped; ACs 1, 3, 4 and 5 remain and are restated below.
A silent self-skip and a recorded deliberate skip are different states, and only the second is
acceptable: this is not closed by adding a comment to the fixture.

## Approach

A **recorded opt-out** becomes the tier's licence not to run, and every non-execution path
consults it.

1. **The record** — `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml`: a TOML declaration with
   `scope = "local-only"`, the deciding ticket id, and a non-blank `reason`. It lives in the
   tree, is greppable, and is what a future reader finds.
2. **The enforcement** — `tests/e2e/_browser_tier.py` exposes `tier_unavailable(detail)`.
   With a complete record it raises a **loud skip** whose reason begins
   `BROWSER TIER DELIBERATELY NOT RUN` and names the record, the deciding ticket and the
   concrete cause. With the record **absent, unparseable, or blank-reasoned** it raises
   `pytest.fail`. Removing the marker therefore turns every browser test RED.
3. **The wiring** — every fixture a browser test depends on replaces its bare
   `pytest.skip(...)` with `tier_unavailable(...)`: `browser_runner`, `editor_server` and
   `editor_server_batch` in `tests/e2e/conftest.py`, **plus** the two in-module server
   fixtures `library_editor_server` and `batch_library_editor_server`, which gate on the same
   `assets_available()` condition and are consumed by browser tests. Leaving those two
   unguarded would keep exactly the silent path this ticket exists to remove.
4. **The summary** — `tier_unavailable` warns through pytest's warnings channel (shown even
   under `-q`, grouped for identical messages), so a reader of a green run is told the tier
   did not run and that this was decided, not missed. The category is
   `pytest.PytestWarning` — an **installed** class, never one defined under `tests/`, because
   an xdist worker serializes a warning by its class's module name and the controller
   re-imports it; a tests-local category is unimportable there and takes the whole session
   down. The per-test skip reason stays short; the warning carries the reasoning in full.
5. **Documentation** — `docs/workflow-editor.md` says all E2E tiers are "opt-in and
   self-skipping", which stops being true; it records the local-only disposition instead. A
   comment in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` beside the e2e provisioning step says
   why no browser-provisioning step exists and points at the record. No workflow step is
   added or removed.

**Portability.** The mechanism reads one repository file: no environment variable, no CI
detection, no provider API. Assume no CI provider is present; nothing branches on one, so a
checkout without CI behaves identically — loud skip with the record, hard failure without it.

**Why not an env-var or a gate script.** An env-var opt-out is per-run configuration, so it is
exactly the state that can be forgotten and revert to an accidental skip; the record must be a
durable tree artefact. A `scripts/check_*.py` gate could only assert the record exists — it
cannot observe that the tier failed to execute, which is what AC3 names. The enforcement has
to sit at the skip site, in the fixture.

## Scope

- `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml` (new) — the recorded opt-out.
- `tests/e2e/_browser_tier.py` (new) — record loader, `tier_unavailable`, the warning channel.
- `tests/e2e/conftest.py` — route the three conftest fixtures through `tier_unavailable`.
- `tests/e2e/test_editor_library.py`, `tests/e2e/test_editor_batch_library.py` — route their
  in-module server fixtures' bare skips through `tier_unavailable`.
- `tests/e2e/test_editor_browser.py` — docstring only ("self-skips" stops being true).
- `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` — its `_replica` helper must copy the guard and
  the record into the sandbox e2e tree (a replica without the record exercises a different
  contract), and its browser skip-reason assertion moves to the new banner.
- `tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py` (new) — the enforcement's own tests.
- `docs/workflow-editor.md` — record the disposition where the tiers are described.
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — comment only.

No `src/rebar` changes: test-infrastructure and documentation work.

## Testing

Moved to a ticket comment to bring the description under the 8,000-character structural
cap, which the completion verifier enforces as a close criterion. Nothing removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] 1. `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml` exists, names the deciding ticket, and states why
      the tier is local-only. Checked by `test_committed_record_is_complete`.
- [x] 3. With the record absent, a browser-tier non-execution FAILS rather than skips. Checked
      by `test_absent_record_fails_instead_of_skipping` and by the manual delete-the-record
      demonstration recorded on this ticket.
- [x] 4. The run's output distinguishes "deliberately not run" from "passed": the skip reason
      begins `BROWSER TIER DELIBERATELY NOT RUN` and a warning carrying that banner appears in
      the warnings summary, without destabilising the run. Checked by
      `test_skip_reason_is_loud_and_names_the_record`,
      `test_a_licensed_non_execution_warns_so_the_summary_shows_it` and
      `test_the_warning_category_is_importable_by_the_xdist_controller`.
- [x] 5. The guard reads only a repository file, so a checkout with no CI provider behaves
      identically. Checked by `test_guard_reads_no_environment_and_knows_no_ci_provider`.
- [x] 6. No e2e module retains an unguarded non-execution path. Checked by
      `test_no_browser_fixture_falls_back_to_a_bare_skip` and
      `test_no_e2e_module_hides_a_test_behind_a_bare_skipif`.
- [x] 7. `pytest tests/e2e tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py -n 2` exits 0 (under xdist,
      which is how CI runs it).
- [x] 8. `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] 9. `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [x] 10. `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists no path under `.github/` other than
      `_build-and-test.yml`, so no ratchet baseline was edited.
